symptoms.name: Yellow Leaves
symptoms.question: Are the leaves turning yellow or pale chlorotic?

symptoms.name: Brown Spots
symptoms.question: Are there distinct brown oval/circular spots visible on the leaves?

symptoms.name: Leaf Drying
symptoms.question: Are the leaf margins or tips drying up and withering?

symptoms.name: Water-Soaked Lesions
symptoms.question: Do you observe translucent, water-soaked streaks or lesions on foliage?

symptoms.name: Spindle-Shaped Spots
symptoms.question: Are spots diamond/spindle-shaped with pointed ends?

symptoms.name: Ash Gray Center
symptoms.question: Do the leaf lesions have a characteristic grayish or whitish center?

symptoms.name: Panicle Rot
symptoms.question: Is there neck rotting or grain discoloration on the panicles?

symptoms.name: Sheath Lesions
symptoms.question: Are there greenish-gray oval lesions banding on the leaf sheath near waterline?

symptoms.name: Stem Lodging
symptoms.question: Is the stem weakened or collapsing (lodging)?

symptoms.name: Orange-Yellow Pustules
symptoms.question: Are powdery orange or yellow pustules present on the leaf surface?

symptoms.name: White Powdery Patches
symptoms.question: Are there white talcum-like powdery patches on leaves or stems?

symptoms.name: Black Powdery Spores
symptoms.question: Are grains replaced by masses of dark black powdery fungal spores?

symptoms.name: Stunted Growth
symptoms.question: Is the plant noticeably stunted in height with delayed development?

symptoms.name: Concentric Rings
symptoms.question: Do leaf spots display concentric circular target-board rings?

symptoms.name: Dark Water-Soaked Spots
symptoms.question: Are dark, rapidly expanding water-soaked spots present on leaves and stems?

symptoms.name: White Mold Underside
symptoms.question: Is there fine white velvety mold growth on the underside of affected leaves?

symptoms.name: Curling Leaves
symptoms.question: Are leaves curling upward and becoming leathery or distorted?

symptoms.name: Whitefly Infestation
symptoms.question: Are small white insects (whiteflies) fluttering when leaves are shaken?

symptoms.name: Fruit Damage
symptoms.question: Are there sunken dark rot patches on the developing fruits?

symptoms.name: Black Stem Rot
symptoms.question: Is the base of the stem turning inky black and rotting?

symptoms.name: Plant Wilting
symptoms.question: Are the plants rapidly wilting and collapsing during warm daytime hours?

symptoms.name: Tuber Rot
symptoms.question: Are harvested tubers showing brownish internal dry rot or foul smelling soft rot?

symptoms.name: Cigar-Shaped Lesions
symptoms.question: Are long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish lesions visible on leaves?

symptoms.name: Cinnamon-Brown Pustules
symptoms.question: Are reddish-brown or cinnamon pustules scattered across both leaf surfaces?

symptoms.name: Angular Leaf Spots
symptoms.question: Are lesions sharply delimited by leaf veinlets, forming angular spots?

symptoms.name: Vascular Browning
symptoms.question: When stem is sliced open, do you see brown discolored vascular bundles?

rice_brown_spot.name: Brown Spot Disease
rice_brown_spot.detailed_treatment: Spray Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Edifenphos (1 ml/L). Correct soil nutrient imbalance with potassium and nitrogen. Ensure proper drainage.
rice_brown_spot.prevention: Treat seeds with Carbendazim (2 g/kg). Use balanced fertilizer application and avoid prolonged water stress.

rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.detailed_treatment: Spray Streptocycline (150 mg/L) combined with Copper Oxychloride (2 g/L). Drain excess standing water from infected fields.
rice_bacterial_leaf_blight.prevention: Grow resistant rice cultivars (e.g., IR64). Avoid high nitrogen top-dressing during disease outbreaks.

rice_blast.name: Rice Blast Disease
rice_blast.detailed_treatment: Foliar spray with Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6 g/L) or Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) at booting and panicle emergence stages.
rice_blast.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization; practice clean seed selection and treat seeds with Tricyclazole.

rice_sheath_blight.name: Sheath Blight Disease
rice_sheath_blight.detailed_treatment: Spray Validamycin 3L (2.5 ml/L) or Hexaconazole 5 EC (2 ml/L) targeted towards the plant base/sheaths.
rice_sheath_blight.prevention: Maintain wider plant spacing to allow ventilation; eliminate alternate weed hosts on field bunds.

wheat_rust.name: Wheat Rust Disease
wheat_rust.detailed_treatment: Apply Propiconazole 25 EC (1 ml/L) or Tebuconazole upon first appearance of pustules.
wheat_rust.prevention: Sow resistant rust-tolerant certified varieties and avoid unseasonably late planting.

wheat_powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
wheat_powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply Wettable Sulfur or Triazole Fungicide
wheat_powdery_mildew.detailed_treatment: Spray Wettable Sulfur (3 g/L) or Triadimefon (1 g/L) covering both upper and lower canopy surfaces.
wheat_powdery_mildew.prevention: Ensure good crop aeration and avoid excessively high seed rates.

wheat_loose_smut.name: Loose Smut Disease
wheat_loose_smut.detailed_treatment: Rogue out infected smutted ear-heads carefully in plastic bags before spores disperse.
wheat_loose_smut.prevention: Solar heat treatment of seeds or chemical dressing with Carboxin / Thiram (2.5 g/kg seed).

tomato_early_blight.name: Early Blight
tomato_early_blight.detailed_treatment: Spray Chlorothalonil (2 g/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L). Prune lower infected leaves touching the soil.
tomato_early_blight.prevention: Mulch soil around plants and stake tomato vines to avoid soil splash.

tomato_late_blight.name: Late Blight
tomato_late_blight.detailed_treatment: Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2 g/L) or Cymoxanil immediately upon dark lesion discovery.
tomato_late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; remove and burn infected plant debris.

tomato_leaf_curl.name: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus
tomato_leaf_curl.pathogen: Tomato Leaf Curl New Delhi Virus (Begomovirus)
tomato_leaf_curl.treatment: Control Whitefly Vectors and Rogue Plants
tomato_leaf_curl.detailed_treatment: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.3 ml/L) or Neem seed kernel extract (5%) to manage whitefly populations.
tomato_leaf_curl.prevention: Install yellow sticky traps (15 traps/acre) and use insect-proof nylon netting in nurseries.

potato_late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
potato_late_blight.detailed_treatment: Foliar spray with Dimethomorph (1 g/L) + Mancozeb (2 g/L) at 7-10 day intervals during cool, humid weather.
potato_late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers; destroy haulms 10 days before harvesting.

potato_blackleg.name: Blackleg and Soft Rot
potato_blackleg.treatment: Apply Copper Bactericide and Improve Drainage
potato_blackleg.detailed_treatment: Drench stem bases with Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L). Avoid handling tubers under wet conditions.
potato_blackleg.prevention: Ensure well-drained planting beds, avoid bruising tubers during harvesting and storage.

maize_northern_leaf_blight.name: Northern Corn Leaf Blight
maize_northern_leaf_blight.detailed_treatment: Apply Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (1 ml/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) at onset of lesions.
maize_northern_leaf_blight.prevention: Rotate with non-host crops (soybean/pulses) and plow under old crop residues.

maize_common_rust.name: Common Rust
maize_common_rust.detailed_treatment: Spray Tebuconazole 250 EC (1 ml/L) if rust lesions appear on upper leaves before silking.
maize_common_rust.prevention: Use resistant maize hybrids and practice early planting to escape peak spore dispersal.

cotton_bacterial_blight.name: Cotton Bacterial Blight
cotton_bacterial_blight.detailed_treatment: Spray Streptocycline (100 mg/L) + Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L) at 12-day intervals.
cotton_bacterial_blight.prevention: Use acid-delinted certified seeds treated with Streptocycline (1 g/kg seed).

cotton_fusarium_wilt.name: Fusarium Wilt
cotton_fusarium_wilt.detailed_treatment: Drench root zone with Carbendazim (1 g/L) or apply biocontrol agent Trichoderma viride enriched in compost.
cotton_fusarium_wilt.prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation; use resistant cotton varieties and balance potash fertilization.

rules.explanation: If crop is Rice and leaves are yellow with brown circular spots and leaf drying, then disease is Brown Spot Disease.
If crop is Rice and leaves exhibit yellowing with water-soaked streaks and marginal leaf drying, then disease is Bacterial Leaf Blight.
If crop is Rice with spindle-shaped spots having ash-gray centers and panicle rot, then disease is Rice Blast Disease.
If crop is Rice with banded lesions on leaf sheath, yellowing leaves, and stem lodging, then disease is Sheath Blight Disease.
If crop is Wheat and orange-yellow powdery pustules occur with leaf chlorosis and drying, then disease is Wheat Rust.

rules.treatment: Apply Wettable Sulfur or Triazole Fungicide
rules.explanation: If crop is Wheat with white powdery fungal patches, yellow leaves, and stunted growth, then disease is Powdery Mildew.
If crop is Wheat and ear heads are transformed into masses of black powdery spores, then disease is Loose Smut.
If crop is Tomato with brown target-like concentric rings on yellowing lower leaves, then disease is Early Blight.
If crop is Tomato with water-soaked lesions, white mold on leaf underside, and fruit rot, then disease is Late Blight.

rules.treatment: Control Whitefly Vectors and Rogue Plants
rules.explanation: If crop is Tomato with upward curling deformed leaves, chlorosis, and whitefly infestation, then disease is Tomato Leaf Curl Virus.
If crop is Potato with rapidly spreading water-soaked leaf spots, foliage drying, and rotting tubers, then disease is Potato Late Blight.

rules.treatment: Apply Copper Bactericide and Improve Drainage
rules.explanation: If crop is Potato with inky black stem rot, yellow leaves, and rapid plant wilting, then disease is Blackleg and Soft Rot.
If crop is Maize with elongated cigar-shaped grayish lesions and extensive leaf drying, then disease is Northern Corn Leaf Blight.
If crop is Maize with scattered cinnamon-brown pustules, brown spots, and leaf drying, then disease is Common Rust.
If crop is Cotton with angular vein-bound leaf spots, black stem cankers, and leaf drying, then disease is Cotton Bacterial Blight.
If crop is Cotton with yellowing leaves, daytime wilting, and brown internal stem vascular discoloration, then disease is Fusarium Wilt.
